points: 1 Attention recipe: 5 local sliding-window layers per global layer with a 1024-token local span (Gemma 2 used 1:1), to cut KV-cache memory; QK-norm replaces soft-capping; GQA with pre/post RMSNorm (p. 1)

2 Long context: 128K tokens (32K for 1B); RoPE base raised from 10k to 1M on global layers only; pre-trained at 32K then scaled to 128K by RoPE rescaling with factor 8; degrades beyond 128K (p. 1, p. 7)

3 Vision: frozen 400M SigLIP encoder at 896x896, shared by 4B/12B/27B (1B has none), 256 soft tokens per image; Pan & Scan is inference-only cropping; P&S gains e.g. 27B DocVQA 85.6 to 90.4, InfoVQA 59.4 to 76.4 (p. 2, p. 8, Table 8)
4 Pre-training: knowledge distillation sampling 256 logits per token; token budgets 14T/12T/4T/2T for 27B/12B/4B/1B; Gemini 2.0 SentencePiece tokenizer, 262k entries (p. 2)
5 Post-training: distillation from a large IT teacher plus RL finetuning on improved BOND/WARM/WARP, with rewards from human-feedback reward models, code execution and ground-truth math (p. 4)

6 Quantization: QAT for about 5,000 steps into per-channel int4, per-block int4 and switched fp8; memory footprints e.g. 27B 54.0 GB bf16 vs 14.1 GB Int4, 72.7 vs 32.8 GB with 32k KV cache (p. 3, Table 3)

7 Chatbot Arena: Gemma-3-27B-IT Elo 1338, rank 9, preliminary (March 8, 2025), vs Gemma-2-27B-it 1220 and larger open models such as DeepSeek-V3 1318, Llama-3.1-405B 1269, Qwen2.5-72B 1257 (p. 4, Table 5)

8 Static zero-shot benchmarks (Table 6) with both baselines, Gemma 2 and Gemini 1.5: e.g. 27B MMLU-Pro 67.5 vs 56.9 (Gemma 2 27B) vs 75.8 (Gemini 1.5 Pro); MATH 89.0 vs 55.6 vs 86.5; external models deliberately not benchmarked (p. 4-5)

9 Ablations: KV-cache overhead 60% for global-only vs under 15% for 1:3 with sw=1024 at 32k context, with minimal perplexity impact from ratio and window size; smaller teacher better for short training, larger teacher better for long training (p. 6-7)

10 Withheld: data mixture and sources, teacher identity and size, post-training data/reward models/hyperparameters; safety violation rates and CBRN knowledge reported only as 'low' with no numbers; memorization 'much lower' with rates only in a figure (p. 2-4, p. 8-10)

errors.quote: 5:1 ratio of local to global attention layers with 1024-token sliding window (vs 1:1 in Gemma 2), reducing KV-cache from 60% to <15% memory overhead at 32k context
errors.paper: The under-15% figure is for a 1:3 configuration with sw=1024, not 5:1: 'reduced to less than 15% with 1:3 and sliding windows of 1024' (Section 5.2, p. 6).

errors.quote: full 32k context KV-cache memory reduced from 60% overhead (global-only) to <15% (5:1 + sw=1024)
errors.paper: Same error repeated: the paper attributes the under-15% overhead to 1:3 with sw=1024 (Section 5.2, p. 6).

errors.quote: Sliding window can reduce to 512 tokens with <0.2 loss
errors.paper: Not in the paper. It says only that 'the sliding window can be reduced significantly without impacting perplexity' (Section 5.2, p. 6); no 512-token or 0.2 figure is printed.

errors.quote: Distillation from larger teacher outperforms smaller teacher after short training
errors.paper: As worded, this is reversed: 'for short training horizons, the smaller teacher is better, but the trend is reversed for longer training' (Section 5.4, p. 7).

errors.quote: significantly lower exact memorization (<0.001% on log scale)
errors.paper: No memorization rate is given in the text; it says only 'a much lower rate than prior models (note the log y-axis)', and Fig. 9 is not readable (Section 6, p. 8).
